data.name: Mikiel
data.gender_notes: Mikiel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Mikael (Mikiel) means ‘Who is like God?’. This name is found in the Bible in both the Old and New Testaments. In the Old Testament, Mikael is the name of an archangel and one of the chief princes. In the New Testament, Saint Michael the Archangel is mentioned as ‘the great prince who stands guard over the people of God’.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies devotion and faith in God.
data.etymology: Mikiel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Who is like God?.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mikiel total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mikael (Mikiel) has been embraced and celebrated in various Christian cultures. It is a popular name in many European and Middle Eastern countries, and in some Latin American countries as well. It is especially revered among the Orthodox Christian community, where Saint Michael the Archangel is one of the most venerated saints. Mikael is also a common name in the Philippines, where he is the patron saint of soldiers, police officers, and paramilitary groups. In various artworks and depictions, Mikael is portrayed as a powerful warrior, riding a white horse and brandishing a sword, standing tall and defiant against the forces of evil.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mikael (Mikiel) holds deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the question posed by God to the archangels, ‘Who is like me?’. This name is a constant reminder of the awe-inspiring power and majesty of God. It is also a call to admire and hold in reverence the heavenly beings who serve as His messengers and protectors. As a personal name, it is an invitation to the bearer to emulate the virtues of the archangel Mikael - courage, strength, and righteousness. It is a powerful reminder that we are not alone in this world, that God and His angels are always with us, watching over us and protecting us from harm.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mikael, meaning "Who is like God?" in Hebrew, symbolizes the deep reverence and awe Christians hold towards the divine. This name is a reminder of God's supremacy and the insignificance of human greatness in comparison. It is also the name of the archangel Michael, a guardian and protector in Christian belief.
